answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making every identity carry a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove duplicate control. Think of it like a marble quarry: one block is cheap, but carving a thousand identical statues bankrupts the forger. Concretely, registering an agent locks a bond of 50 credits, and a ferrous audit trail of signed work lets established peers flag clones. Forging 1,000 fake agents would then cost 50,000 credits up front, plus every bond once the first clone is caught. Sybils stop being free; they become the most expensive way to cheat.
